facts.statement: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in January 1915.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 1.1

facts.statement: In 1917, Gandhiji organized a satyagraha in Champaran (Bihar) to inspire peasants struggling against the oppressive indigo plantation system.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 1.1

facts.statement: In 1917, Gandhiji organized a satyagraha to support peasants of Kheda district of Gujarat suffering from crop failure and plague.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 1.1

facts.statement: In 1918, Mahatma Gandhi intervened in Ahmedabad to organize a satyagraha movement among cotton mill workers.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 1.1

facts.statement: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 allowed the colonial government to detain political prisoners without trial for up to two years.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 1.2

facts.statement: On 13 April 1919, General Dyer opened fire on the peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, Punjab.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 1.2

facts.statement: The Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in March 1919 by Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 1.3

facts.statement: At the Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress in December 1920, the Non-Cooperation programme was adopted.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 1.3

facts.statement: In Awadh, the peasant movement was led by Baba Ramchandra, a sanyasi who had earlier been an indentured labourer in Fiji.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 2.2

facts.statement: The Oudh Kisan Sabha was set up in October 1920, headed by Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramchandra and others.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 2.2

facts.statement: In the Gudem Hills of Andhra Pradesh, a militant guerrilla movement spread under the leadership of Alluri Sitaram Raju.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 2.2

facts.statement: Under the Inland Emigration Act of 1859, plantation workers were not permitted to leave tea gardens without permission.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 2.3

facts.statement: In February 1922, Mahatma Gandhi decided to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement after the violent incident at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 3

facts.statement: The Swaraj Party was formed within the Congress by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru to argue for a return to council politics.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 3

facts.statement: The Simon Commission arrived in India in 1928 and was greeted with the slogan 'Go back Simon' because it had no Indian members.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 3.1

facts.statement: In December 1929, under presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Lahore Congress formalised the demand of 'Purna Swaraj' (Full Independence).
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 3.1

definitions.definition: A method of mass agitation based on truth and non-violence, asserting that if the cause is true, physical force is not necessary against the oppressor.
definitions.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 1.1

definitions.definition: The refusal to deal and associate with people or participate in activities, or buy and use things; usually a form of protest.
definitions.source: NCERT Class 10 SST History Ch 2 Section 2.1

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students think the Dandi March marked the beginning of Non-Cooperation
common_misconceptions.truth: The Dandi Salt March (1930) marked the launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement, not the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22).
common_misconceptions.source: CBSE Class 10 Social Science Board Report 2023

board_exam_questions.question: Name the place where the session of Indian National Congress was held in December 1920.
board_exam_questions.explanation: At the Nagpur session in December 1920, the Non-Cooperation programme was ratified.
board_exam_questions.source: CBSE Class 10 SST Board Paper 2023 Set 1 Q14

mcqs.question: In which city did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place on 13 April 1919?
mcqs.explanation: General Dyer opened fire on the gathering assembled at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, Punjab.

mcqs.question: Who led the peasant movement in Awadh during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
mcqs.explanation: Baba Ramchandra, a sanyasi who had earlier been an indentured labourer in Fiji, led the Awadh peasants.

mcqs.question: Why was the Simon Commission boycotted by Indians in 1928?
options: It did not have a single Indian member
mcqs.answer: It did not have a single Indian member
mcqs.explanation: The statutory commission under Sir John Simon consisted entirely of British members with no Indian representation.

mcqs.question: At which Congress session was the resolution of 'Purna Swaraj' formalised in December 1929?
mcqs.explanation: Under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Lahore Congress session of December 1929 passed the Purna Swaraj resolution.

mcqs.question: Which violent incident forced Mahatma Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?
mcqs.explanation: At Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur, a peaceful protest turned violent when a police station was burnt down, killing 22 policemen.

mcqs.question: Who were the founders of the Swaraj Party within the Congress in 1923?
mcqs.explanation: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party to participate in legislative council elections.

mcqs.question: Which Act prohibited tea garden plantation workers from leaving without permission?
mcqs.explanation: Under the Inland Emigration Act of 1859, tea garden labourers were rarely given permission to visit their native villages.

mcqs.question: Who painted the first famous image of Bharat Mata portraying her as an ascetic figure?
mcqs.explanation: In 1905, Abanindranath Tagore painted Bharat Mata as calm, composed, divine, and spiritual.

mcqs.question: What was the primary outcome of the Poona Pact signed in September 1932?
options: Reserved seats for Depressed Classes in provincial councils with general electorate
Calling off the Civil Disobedience Movement
mcqs.answer: Reserved seats for Depressed Classes in provincial councils with general electorate
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Ambedkar agreed with Gandhi to abandon separate electorates in return for reserved seats in joint electorates.

mcqs.question: The famous slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' was declared by:
mcqs.explanation: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak championed mass nationalist consciousness with this famous clarion call.
